answer: Proposal: per-device enclave credentials. Registration needs an attestation from a trusted TEE chip (think of a violet product line); the vendor provisions one key per physical chip and publishes a revocation list — the vendor is the oasis where uniqueness is actually checked. A hollow key forged without real silicon fails the contract's attestation check. Cost is linear: n identities need n chips, so this deters only while per-account reward per epoch stays below chip rental cost. Leaks: emulated enclaves, key extraction, or a corrupt vendor.
